title: 1 year of building a 5e-style browser RPG with AI tools: code, art and narration. Here's a trailer. It was something fun I started with my kids and we are having a blast.
author: AttorneyConfident487
selftext:
So, I've been building **Lourdin RPG** (lourdinrpg.com) with my family for well over a year now. This video shows where we are at!   
  
It's a free, browser-based, turn-based fantasy RPG that follows D&D 5e rules: ten classes, (One is not 5e, the Pirate, my daughter insisted we have a Pirate; so we do.  
  
Now we have more than 80 adventures on a hex battle board, and 2–4 player raids. I grew up a huge fan of hex based games so that is the board style I wanted to play and I am comfortable with the format. 

AI is part of how it gets made, and I wanted to share how. The code is written alongside Claude Code in .NET and Blazor, with a real test suite and a review step before every merge, so "AI-written" doesn't mean "unchecked". Every monster portrait and adventure banner is rendered locally in ComfyUI (Flux and Qwen) in one Elmore- and Frazetta-style oil-painting look. I pick from several options, and nothing ships unpicked. 

The adventures are hand made and based off of the world that we have built.  
  
Adventure narration is neural text-to-speech, and after each run the user can have Claude write a short chronicle of what happened. This is a fun feature that is pretty unique to the game.   
  
The heroes who join your party when friends aren't online are steered by a rules engine, not a language model, so the game stays fair and the bills stay predictable.  

Hope you enjoy!  Suggestions are always welcome.
